Models/AppData.cs:
Addressed statically

Although AppData implements IAppDataService, the rest of the code goes straight to the static fields. The explicit interface implementations at the top of the class only forward to those same static members.
Views/Controls/MediaPlayerControl.axml.c:
File name

The file is called .axml.cs, not .axaml.cs. A <DependentUpon> entry in the csproj is what links it to the markup.
Models/DatabaseOperations.cs:
All methods static

Database is a plain class that is never instantiated; every operation is a static method. Each one sets its own headers and creates its own HttpClient. Which key it sends depends on the route: X-Admin-Key for the ones the server guards with the admin key, X-User-Key for the per-user routes, and Auth with the user identifier in nearly all of them.
Models/AppConfig.cs:
The default config ships a key

BuildDefault() writes an encrypted literal client key into a fresh config.json. DPAPI only protects it at rest on that machine — the plaintext is in the source, so treat it as a shared installation secret rather than a per-user one.
Models/MediaConverter.cs:
Copy before re-encode

The container tables exist so a stream that already fits the target is passed through with copy. Only a mismatch triggers a re-encode, which is why converting an .mkv holding AAC into .mp4 is close to instant while the same file with Vorbis is not.
Models/ApiClient.cs:
GetFileFromStream builds the path by concatenation

The target is path + fileName, with fileName from Content-Disposition. Neither caller passes a directory with a trailing separator, so the file lands next to the intended folder with a glued name. Path.Combine fixes it.
